objectives: Hear /s/ followed immediately by /l/ at the beginning of a taught word.
Blend /s/ and /l/ smoothly without inserting a vowel between them.
Distinguish the initial sl blend from /s/ alone and other taught blends.
Say the complete word after blending the onset with the remaining sounds.
concepts: The initial sl blend contains /s/ followed by /l/.
Both consonant sounds remain audible in the blend.
No extra vowel belongs between /s/ and /l/.
Listening for the complete word confirms accurate blending.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the beginning of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
Joining speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Slip starts with /s/ followed by /l/; sun starts with /s/ alone.
Keep /s/ and /l/ together, then blend the rest of the word.

commonMistakes: Adding a vowel and saying suh-lip instead of blending smoothly.
Leaving out /l/ and saying sip for slip.
Guessing before hearing the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Do not insert a vowel between the consonants.
Blend the onset with the rest of the word.
Check the complete word against the sounds.
revisionPoints: Slip and slim both begin with sl.
